- When sentiment is predominantly positive (≥ 1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion bias.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots in subsequent days; apply downward correction to avoid overreaction.
- If sentiment includes negative signals (e.g., -1.0 or 0.0), model frequently underestimates; increase forecast by 2–5% to compensate for bearish sentiment lag.
- Model exhibits persistent lag in capturing true price momentum; adjust forecast to be 1–2 days ahead of actual trend, especially in high volatility periods.
- In multi-day forecast horizons, model underestimates late-period (last 5–10 days) price movements; apply upward bias to final 5–7 days if sentiment remains positive.
- When sentiment is mixed or neutral, model tends to average out; use weighted smoothing based on sentiment strength to avoid flat forecasts.
